1.6 Age Distributions of Offenders

The distributions for the last decade, where available, are shown next. While NIBRS data is available for years prior to 2023, it only reached 80% coverage for police agencies that year and hence is not representative of the United States.

In the above age distributions, a child is younger than the age of criminal responsibility for each jurisdiction, a juvenile has passed the age of criminal responsibility but is younger than the age of legal majority, and an adult has passed the age of legal majority. The per-country thresholds are:

Age of Criminal
Country Responsibility Age of Majority
Australia 10 (Not in VIC, ACT) 18
Germany 14 18
New Zealand 10 20
Spain 14 18
United States 11 (Federal Law) 18

Age thresholds for criminal responsibility are 12 in Victoria (VIC) and 14 in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT). They vary widely amongst U.S. states, with 24 of them not having one.

The per-country data sources are:

  • Australian Institute of Criminology, notably sr 51
  • The Bundeskriminalamt's polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik, notably tables on suspects and incidents — good luck accessing any material on that website, since most requests simply time out
  • policedata.nz, notably proceedings (offender demographics)
  • The Ministerio del Interior's annual series on crime, arrests/investigated
  • The FBI's National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS)
